claims: The 25th Amendment addresses succession in Section 1.
The 25th Amendment addresses filling vice president vacancies in Section 2.
The 25th Amendment addresses voluntary transfer of power in Section 3.
The 25th Amendment addresses involuntary removal by the Cabinet in Section 4.

The 25th Amendment was ratified following President John F. Kennedy's assassination to clarify ambiguities in Article II regarding presidential inability and succession, as outlined in the Library of Congress – Constitution Annotated.
LII | Legal Information Institute states that Section 1 of the 25th Amendment confirms the Vice President becomes President if the President dies, resigns, or is removed.
Section 2 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to nominate a new Vice President, subject to Congressional confirmation.

Section 3 of the 25th Amendment allows the President to declare in writing they are unable to perform duties, making the Vice President Acting President until a written declaration of recovery is made.

The National Constitution Center states that Section 4 of the 25th Amendment allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President unable to serve, transferring power to the Vice President.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1973 when Ford replaced Agnew.
The 25th Amendment was used in 1974 when Ford became President and Rockefeller became Vice President.
The 25th Amendment was used for temporary transfers for medical procedures by President Reagan.
The 25th Amendment was used for temporary transfers for medical procedures by President Bush.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment ensures that if the President contests their removal, Congress has the authority to decide the issue.
